{{Recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Japan|Cuisine of Japan]]

'''Sashimi''' is raw meat, sliced very thin. It is typically served with [[Cookbook:Onigiri|onigiri]] or [[Cookbook:Sushi|sushi]]. Although the meat used is usually a kind of [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]], [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] can also be used.

== Ingredients ==
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] fillet (e.g. [[Cookbook:Salmon|salmon]], [[Cookbook:Tuna|tuna]], etc.)

== Procedure ==

# [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] fish as thinly as possible across the grain to keep it tender, like you would a steak.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Since the fish is raw, it is important that it be as fresh as possible.
* Some people avoid freshwater fish (e.g. freshwater [[Cookbook:Eel|eel]], [[Cookbook:Salmon|salmon]]) entirely for sashimi, because they may contain parasites that do not live in saltwater.
* [[Cookbook:Eel|Eel's]] blood contains a toxin, and eel needs to be cooked to break down the toxin.
